FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_RA_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment` does not define a total deterministic tie-break for exact score ties. In `assign()`, if PM/COL scores and `_tie_break_key()` are equal, Python falls back to input order; reversing the same homogeneous model list changes the chosen PM. In `reassign()`, `best_col_id = max(col_scores, ...)` has no tie-break at all, and because `remaining_ids` comes from an unordered `set`, equal-score COL selection can flip across processes.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make role selection use a total order independent of container order. Add a final canonical discriminator such as `model_id` to the selection key, and in `reassign()` choose from a stable list of `ModelSpec`s using `(adjusted_score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)` instead of `max()` over a dict built from a set.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_RA_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` does not honor its `active_models` contract. When `active_models is None`, it uses `set(self.role_map.keys())`, not the full managed pool, so once a model drops out of `role_map` the default path can never reintroduce it even though the docstring says “all models active.” Separately, `new_map` is initialized with the locked PM unconditionally, so `reassign(..., {'x'})` still returns a map containing the PM even when the caller explicitly said the PM was inactive.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Keep a separate authoritative managed-id set and validate `active_models` against it. If `active_models is None`, derive from all managed models or a dedicated active-set source, not from the last role map. If PM must always be active, raise on omission instead of silently re-adding it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_RA_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: `capability_scores` is populated only in `assign()` and never refreshed in `reassign()`. After live-fingerprint reassignment, `role_map` can change but `get_ordering()` still returns the original scores and still includes now-inactive models. I verified a case where live fingerprints flip COL from `y` to `x`, while `get_ordering(Role.COL)` still reports the old `y > x` ordering.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute `capability_scores` during `reassign()`, or make `get_ordering()` compute current scores on demand from the current scoring pool and optionally filter to active models.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_RA_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` assumes `model_id` is unique but never checks it. Because internal state is keyed by `model_id`, duplicates silently overwrite `capability_scores` and `_failure_history`, and `role_map` can end up with fewer entries than `self._models`. Verified example: three `ModelSpec`s with IDs `dup`, `dup`, `other` produce a two-entry `role_map` and drop one physical model entirely.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate uniqueness of `model_id` before any maps are built and raise `ValueError` on duplicates.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_RA_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: `_capability_score()` claims to return a scalar in `[0, 1]`, but `CapabilityFingerprint` has no range validation, so invalid inputs can generate scores above 1 or below 0. Verified example: a model with negative fingerprint components produced PM/COL/PAR scores of `1.3125`, `1.625`, and `1.9375`. This breaks the stated scoring contract and can distort role selection.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `CapabilityFingerprint.__post_init__()` validation enforcing the documented bounds (`D_decay >= 0`; `v_bar`, `A`, `C` within their allowed range) and fail fast on invalid data.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_RA_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.43  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.31  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig.theta_col` is exposed as a Role Assignment parameter and documented as enabling threshold-based COL selection, but the Role Assignment area never reads it. That leaves dead public configuration surface and misleading behavior for callers who expect it to matter.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `theta_col` from the public config or implement the documented threshold-based COL path and test it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
